fixes.explanation: Seventy scouts, friend? That's not a spy mission, that's a tour group with matching T-shirts. Moses picks twelve, one from each tribe (Deut 1:23). Each tribe gets one man on the trail, and nobody has to carry a clipboard for seventy.

Weapons aren't what the text puts in their hands. It says the spies “…took some of the fruit of the land in their hands, carried it down to us…” That's the souvenir the verse names. Nothing here says they brought back anything from the Amorites.

Waiting for another sign isn't in the passage. The text says the people “…would not listen.” They “…presumptuously went up into the hill country.” That's quite a change from a crowd that was unwilling to go up before (Deut 1:26). A second sign never comes up.

problems.problem: The joke about the number fitting in one verse makes the way Scripture is written the joke.
The text says the scouts carried fruit, but does not say they carried nothing else. It also does not say the scouts were excluded when the people later armed themselves.
Calling their change of action 'a lot of speed' suggests how quickly it happened, which the text does not say.
